body:
GFH Bank has closed its $63 million Power Systems Opportunities Fund, investing in electricity infrastructure businesses MacLean Power Systems (MPS) and H&MV Engineering across North America and Europe through vehicles managed by Pathway Capital Management and SQ Capital, respectively.

The Sharia-compliant fund targets businesses supplying equipment and engineering services for electricity grids, according to GFH’s bourse filing on Sunday.

GFHexpects the closing to improve its financial performance and investment returns. The company did not quantify the expected financial impact or disclose how it split the capital between the two investments.

MPS manufactures components used in electricity transmission, distribution, and substations. In March 2026, the company merged with Power Grid Components in a Blackstone-led transaction, with Blackstone-affiliated funds becoming the majority owner and a Centerbridge affiliate reinvesting.

Meanwhile, H&MV designs and builds high-voltage infrastructure for data centers, battery energy storage, utilities, and renewable energy projects. The Irish engineering company expects fiscal 2026 revenue of about $1.12 billion (€1 billion), up from $68.4 million in 2020, and targets annual revenue of $3.36 billion within five years.

H&MV also reported a $2.2 billion order book and a $ 17.9 billion pipeline of potential projects.

In August 2026, Exponent announced the closing of an $840.6 million continuation vehicle for H&MV, valuing the company at nearly $1.6 billion. Apollo S3, Pantheon, and SQ Capital joined the investment structure.

GFH Chief Investment Officer Hammad Younas said the investments would provide exposure to maintaining existing electricity networks and building additional capacity, driven by demand from artificial intelligence (AI), data centers, and electrification.

H&MV’s plans include growing its US operations, hiring additional employees, and pursuing acquisitions, according to its August funding announcement. The company had more than 1,900 employees across 20 international offices when GFH announced the investment.

GFH reported more than $25 billion in assets and funds under management in its October disclosure. The Bahrain-headquartered bank is listed on Bahrain Bourse, Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange, Boursa Kuwait, and Dubai Financial Market.

GFH Group CEO Hisham Alrayes ranked eighth on Forbes Middle East’s Top 50 Asset Managers 2026 and 86th on its Top 100 CEOs 2026.
